title: Feel better!
pair_game: Point at a picture. Say the problem. Your partner gives advice: “You should …”. Then swap!

grammar_box.title: You should … / Don't …
grammar_box.tip: After should use the simple verb: You should rest. (NOT You should to rest.)

questions: Are you feeling sick or tired?
What do you do when you have a cold?
Do you stay home from school when you are sick?
Who takes care of you when you are not well?
Do you eat healthy food every day?
How many hours do you sleep at night?
Do you exercise or play sports to stay healthy?
What makes you feel better when you are sad?
starters: Yes, I feel a bit … . / No, I feel fine.
When I have a cold I … and I drink … .
Yes, I stay at home. / No, I go to school because … .
My … takes care of me. He/She … .
Yes, I eat … every day. / No, I should eat more … .
I sleep about … hours every night.
Yes, I play … . / No, but I should … .
When I am sad, … makes me feel better.
Yes, I am happy today because … . / No, because … .
samples: What do you do when you have a cold?
I stay in bed and I drink hot tea with lemon. My mother gives me **medicine** and I **rest** for two days.
Who takes care of you when you are not well?
My mother takes care of me. She makes soup and says, “**You should** sleep!” My grandmother brings me honey.
How many hours do you sleep at night?
I sleep about eight hours. On school days I go to bed at ten and I get up at six.

survey.title: Class survey
survey.question: How many hours do you sleep at night?

game.title: Give good advice!
game.rules: Move your counter. Read the problem. Give advice with “You should …”. Good advice? Move again!

mini_talk.title: Feel better!
mini_talk.model: Today I feel very well, thank you! But last month I was **ill**. I had a **headache** and a **temperature**, so I did not go to school. My mother took me to the **doctor** and he gave me **medicine**. He said, “**Rest** for three days and drink a lot of water.” Now I feel much **better**. My advice: **you should** sleep eight hours every night!
